title: NEET UG
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public NEET UG syllabus. Not a capture of past questions.

items.stem: Which cell organelle is bounded by a double membrane and carries out the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis?
items.explanation: The chloroplast is enclosed by a double membrane and its internal thylakoid membranes host the light-dependent reactions. Mitochondria carry out respiration, peroxisomes are single-membraned, and ribosomes are not membrane bound.

items.stem: The specific region of an enzyme at which the substrate binds and the reaction is catalysed is called the
items.explanation: The active site is a pocket whose shape and charge complement the substrate so that the reaction is accelerated. An allosteric site binds regulators, a prosthetic group is a tightly bound cofactor, and the apoenzyme is the protein part of a holoenzyme.

items.stem: In C4 plants the primary carbon dioxide acceptor in the mesophyll cells is
items.explanation: In C4 mesophyll cells the enzyme PEP carboxylase fixes carbon dioxide onto phosphoenolpyruvate to give the four-carbon oxaloacetate. Ribulose bisphosphate is the acceptor in the C3 Calvin cycle, while oxaloacetate and glucose are products or intermediates.

items.stem: The net gain of ATP when one molecule of glucose is converted into two molecules of pyruvate by glycolysis is
items.explanation: Glycolysis produces four ATP molecules but consumes two during the preparatory phase, giving a net gain of two ATP per glucose. The value four ignores the investment, thirty-six is the total aerobic yield, and zero would mean no substrate-level phosphorylation.

items.stem: In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous parents of genotype RrYy, the fraction of offspring expected to show both recessive traits is
items.explanation: Each recessive trait appears with probability 1/4 in a monohybrid cross, so both together give 1/4 times 1/4 = 1/16. The value 9/16 is the double dominant class, 3/16 is one dominant and one recessive, and 1/4 is a single-trait probability.

items.stem: A man of blood group AB marries a woman of blood group O. The possible blood groups of their children are
items.explanation: The father can pass on the IA or the IB allele while the mother can only pass on i, so children are heterozygous IAi (group A) or IBi (group B). Group AB cannot arise because the mother contributes no AB allele, and group O occurs only when both parents contribute i.

items.stem: The two strands of a DNA double helix are held together by hydrogen bonds formed between
items.explanation: Hydrogen bonds link complementary bases, adenine with thymine and guanine with cytosine, across the helix. Sugar and phosphate form the covalent backbone, purines pair with pyrimidines rather than each other, and phosphate groups are joined by phosphodiester bonds.

items.stem: During DNA replication the enzyme that adds nucleotides to the growing new strand is
items.explanation: DNA polymerase extends the new strand by adding nucleotides complementary to the template. Ligase seals nicks between fragments, helicase unwinds the duplex, and primase lays down the short RNA primer that polymerase then extends.

items.stem: During transcription in a eukaryotic cell the enzyme RNA polymerase synthesises a strand of
options: RNA using DNA as the template
DNA using RNA as the template
Protein using messenger RNA as the template
DNA using DNA as the template
items.explanation: Transcription copies one DNA strand into a complementary RNA strand. Making DNA from RNA is reverse transcription, making protein from messenger RNA is translation, and copying DNA from DNA is replication.

items.stem: The organelle that serves as the site of protein synthesis in a living cell is the
items.explanation: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into polypeptide chains. The nucleus stores DNA, the Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins, and lysosomes carry out intracellular digestion.

items.stem: The enzyme present in human saliva that begins the digestion of starch is
items.explanation: Salivary amylase hydrolyses starch into maltose in the mouth. Pepsin digests proteins in the stomach, trypsin digests proteins in the small intestine, and lipase acts on fats.

items.stem: The maximum volume of air that a person can exhale after a maximum inspiration is called the
items.explanation: Vital capacity is the sum of tidal volume, inspiratory reserve volume and expiratory reserve volume, the largest volume that can be moved in one breath. Tidal volume is a resting breath, residual volume stays in the lungs, and inspiratory reserve volume is only the extra inspired air.

items.stem: The valve that separates the left atrium from the left ventricle in the human heart is the
items.explanation: The bicuspid or mitral valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle. The tricuspid valve guards the right atrioventricular opening, while the pulmonary and aortic semilunar valves guard the exits of the right and left ventricles.

items.stem: The structural and functional unit of the human kidney is the
items.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, the units that filter blood and form urine. A neuron is the nerve cell, an alveolus is a lung air sac, and a villus is a fold of the intestinal wall.

items.stem: The junction between two adjacent neurons across which a nerve impulse is transmitted is called a
items.explanation: At a synapse the axon terminal releases neurotransmitters that carry the signal to the next neuron. The node of Ranvier and myelin sheath affect conduction along one axon, and a dendrite is the receiving process of a neuron.

items.stem: The hormone secreted by the thyroid gland that regulates the basal metabolic rate of the body is
items.explanation: Thyroxine raises the rate of oxygen consumption and heat production, thus setting the basal metabolic rate. Insulin regulates blood glucose, adrenaline is a fight-or-flight hormone of the adrenal medulla, and cortisol comes from the adrenal cortex.

items.stem: In human reproduction the event in which the sperm nucleus fuses with the egg nucleus is known as
items.explanation: Fertilisation is the fusion of the haploid sperm and egg nuclei to form a diploid zygote. Implantation is the embedding of the embryo in the uterus, ovulation is the release of the egg, and cleavage is the division of the zygote.

items.stem: In angiosperms the male gametes are carried to the embryo sac through the
items.explanation: After a pollen grain germinates it grows a pollen tube that carries the two male gametes to the embryo sac for double fertilisation. Phloem and vascular bundles conduct food and water, while the stigma is only the receptive surface where the pollen lands.

items.stem: The upward movement of water from the roots to the leaves of a tall tree is mainly driven by
items.explanation: Evaporation of water from leaves creates a tension that pulls a continuous column of water up the xylem, a mechanism called the transpiration pull. Root pressure can only push water a short distance, xylem transport is passive, and guttation is the loss of liquid water from leaf margins.

items.stem: The macronutrient that is a constituent of chlorophyll, proteins and nucleic acids is
items.explanation: Nitrogen is part of chlorophyll, amino acids and nucleotides and is a macronutrient required in large amounts. Iron, zinc and boron are micronutrients needed only in traces.

items.stem: The underground stem of ginger that stores food and bears nodes and internodes is a
items.explanation: Ginger is a rhizome, a horizontal underground stem with nodes, internodes and scaly leaves. A bulb is made of fleshy scales as in onion, a tuber is a swollen tip as in potato, and a corm is a solid swollen stem base as in colocasia.

items.stem: The simple plant tissue that provides mechanical strength and is made of dead cells with thick lignified walls is
items.explanation: Sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity and have heavily lignified secondary walls that give rigidity. Parenchyma is living and thin walled, collenchyma has unevenly thickened living cells, and phloem is a complex conducting tissue.

items.stem: The stage of mitosis at which the chromosomes line up along the equator of the cell is
items.explanation: During metaphase the chromosomes arrange on the metaphase plate at the cell equator before separating. Prophase shows condensing chromosomes, anaphase shows the chromatids moving to the poles, and telophase shows the nuclei re-forming.

items.stem: If the energy available at the producer level of an ecosystem is 10000 J, the energy transferred to the secondary consumers under the ten percent law is
items.explanation: Ten percent of producer energy, 1000 J, reaches the primary consumers, and ten percent of that, 100 J, reaches the secondary consumers. The values 1000 J and 10 J belong to the primary and tertiary levels, and 10000 J would mean no loss at all.

items.stem: The relationship in which one organism benefits while the other is neither harmed nor benefited is called
items.explanation: In commensalism one partner gains an advantage while the other is unaffected, as when an orchid grows on a tree. In mutualism both benefit, in parasitism one is harmed, and predation involves killing and eating the other.

items.stem: The variety and variability of living organisms present at all levels of biological organisation is called
items.explanation: Biodiversity refers to the range of life from genes to ecosystems. Taxonomy is the science of naming and classifying organisms, ecology studies interactions with the environment, and evolution deals with descent with modification.

items.stem: Forelimbs of a whale, a bat and a human share the same basic bone plan and therefore provide evidence for
items.explanation: Such homologous structures share a common ancestry and show that species diverged to adapt to different uses. Convergent evolution produces analogous organs with different origins, while the other two are discredited ideas.

items.stem: The disease caused by a protozoan and transmitted by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito is
items.explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium species and spread by the female Anopheles mosquito. Dengue and filariasis are transmitted by Aedes and Culex mosquitoes respectively, and plague is a bacterial disease spread by fleas.

items.stem: Which of the following blood cells is responsible for producing antibodies against a foreign antigen?
items.explanation: B lymphocytes differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies in the humoral immune response. T lymphocytes mediate cell-mediated immunity, erythrocytes carry oxygen, and thrombocytes help in clotting.

items.stem: The laboratory technique used to amplify a specific segment of DNA into millions of copies in vitro is
items.explanation: The polymerase chain reaction uses repeated cycles of denaturation, primer annealing and extension to amplify DNA. Gel electrophoresis separates fragments by size, ELISA detects antigens or antibodies, and centrifugation separates by density.

items.stem: The number of moles of oxygen atoms present in one mole of carbon dioxide is
items.explanation: Each molecule of carbon dioxide contains two oxygen atoms, so one mole provides two moles of oxygen atoms. One mole of the molecule and one mole of the element are not the same, and three or four ignore the formula CO2.

items.stem: The mass of water produced when one mole of methane is completely burnt in excess oxygen is (molar mass of water = 18 g per mol)
items.explanation: The equation CH4 + 2O2 gives CO2 + 2H2O shows that one mole of methane gives two moles of water, that is 2 times 18 = 36 g. The value 18 g would be only one mole of water, 44 g is the mass of the carbon dioxide formed, and 16 g is the mass of methane used.

items.stem: The quantum number that determines the orientation of an orbital in space is the
items.explanation: The magnetic quantum number fixes the orbital orientation along the axes. The principal quantum number gives the shell and energy, the azimuthal quantum number gives the subshell shape, and the spin quantum number describes electron spin.

items.stem: Which of the following elements has the smallest atomic radius?
items.explanation: Across a period the effective nuclear charge rises while electrons enter the same shell, so the radius falls from sodium to silicon. Potassium lies in the next period and is the largest of the four.

items.stem: According to the VSEPR theory the shape of the methane molecule is
items.explanation: Carbon in methane has four bonding pairs and no lone pair, which arrange themselves as far apart as possible at about 109 degrees, giving a tetrahedral shape. Square planar, trigonal planar and linear shapes need different numbers of electron pairs.

items.stem: For an exothermic reaction carried out at constant pressure the sign of the enthalpy change is
items.explanation: An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy of the system falls and the change is negative. A positive value would indicate an endothermic reaction, and a zero value would mean no heat change at all.

items.stem: In the equilibrium reaction N2 plus 3H2 in equilibrium with 2NH3, an increase in pressure at constant temperature will
options: Shift the equilibrium towards the products
Shift the equilibrium towards the reactants
Have no effect on the equilibrium
items.explanation: By Le Chatelier's principle, raising the pressure shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas, which is the products with two moles against four on the left. The reverse shift, no effect, or complete stoppage are all contrary to the principle.

items.stem: The colligative property that is commonly used to determine the molar mass of a non-volatile solute is
items.explanation: Colligative properties such as boiling point elevation depend on the number of solute particles and can be related to molar mass. Colour, viscosity and refractive index are not colligative properties.

items.stem: The SI unit of molar conductivity of an electrolyte solution is
items.explanation: Molar conductivity is conductivity divided by concentration, so its SI unit is siemens metre squared per mole. S cm^-1 and S m^-1 are units of conductivity itself, and ohm cm is a unit of resistivity.

items.stem: The observation that the rate constant of a reaction is strongly affected by temperature is best explained by the
items.explanation: The Arrhenius equation expresses the rate constant as a function of temperature through the activation energy. Le Chatelier's principle concerns equilibrium shifts, while Hund's rule and the Markownikoff rule are unrelated to reaction kinetics.

items.stem: The IUPAC name of the compound CH3CH2OH is
items.explanation: A two-carbon chain bearing a hydroxyl group is named ethanol. Methanol has one carbon, ethanal is the aldehyde with a carbonyl group, and ethanoic acid contains a carboxyl group.

items.stem: The reagent that converts an alkene into the corresponding alkane by addition of hydrogen is
options: H2 in the presence of a nickel catalyst
items.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation adds hydrogen across the double bond using a nickel, platinum or palladium catalyst. Bromine water and acidified permanganate oxidise or add halogens rather than saturate the bond, and sodium hydroxide does not add hydrogen.

items.stem: The compound formed when ethanol is oxidised by acidified potassium dichromate is
items.explanation: A primary alcohol such as ethanol is first oxidised to the aldehyde and then to ethanoic acid by acidified dichromate. Ethene is formed by dehydration, ethane by reduction, and methanol is a different one-carbon alcohol.

items.stem: The oxidation state of iron in the complex ion [Fe(CN)6]3- is
items.explanation: Six cyanide ligands contribute a total charge of -6 and the overall charge is -3, so iron must carry +3. A value of +2 would give an overall charge of -4, and the other values do not balance the charges.

items.stem: The linkage that joins the two monosaccharide units of sucrose together is a
items.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide in which glucose and fructose are joined by a glycosidic bond formed by loss of water. A peptide bond joins amino acids, an ester bond appears in fats, and a hydrogen bond is a weak non-covalent interaction.

items.stem: The SI unit of magnetic flux density, the tesla, is equivalent to
items.explanation: From the expression F = B I L sin(theta), the tesla equals newton per ampere metre, which reduces to kg s^-2 A^-1. The other options contain extra or missing powers of length and time.

items.stem: A body starting from rest moves with a uniform acceleration of 4 m per second squared. The distance travelled in 3 seconds is
items.explanation: Using s = ut + (1/2)at^2 with u = 0 gives s = 0.5 times 4 times 9 = 18 m. Using at^2 without the factor one half gives 36 m, and using at gives 12 m at one second.

items.stem: A projectile is launched at an angle of 45 degrees with a speed of 20 m per second. Its horizontal range is (g = 10 m per second squared)
items.explanation: The range R = u^2 sin(2 theta) / g = 400 times sin 90 degrees / 10 = 40 m. Forgetting the sine term or the factor of two in the angle leads to the other values.

items.stem: A constant force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg. The acceleration produced is
items.explanation: By Newton's second law a = F/m = 10/2 = 5 m per second squared. Multiplying instead of dividing gives 20, and inverting or misreading the ratio gives the other distractors.

items.stem: A body of mass 2 kg is lifted vertically to a height of 5 m. The work done against gravity is (g = 10 m per second squared)
items.explanation: Work done against gravity is m g h = 2 times 10 times 5 = 100 J. Omitting the mass, the height or the factor of the gravitational acceleration produces the other values.

items.stem: At a height above the Earth's surface equal to the Earth's radius, the acceleration due to gravity becomes
options: One half of its surface value
One fourth of its surface value
items.explanation: Using g' = g R^2 / (R + h)^2 with h = R gives g' = g/4. A height equal to the radius doubles the distance from the centre, and the inverse square law reduces the acceleration to a quarter.

items.stem: The time period of a simple pendulum of length L executing small oscillations on the Earth's surface is
options: 2 pi times the square root of g/L
pi times the square root of L/g
2 pi times the square root of L/g
items.explanation: The restoring force per unit displacement gives T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g). Inverting the ratio or using L/g without the square root gives the wrong expressions.

items.stem: Sound waves are mechanical waves and therefore cannot travel through
items.explanation: Sound needs a material medium to transmit its compressions and rarefactions, so it cannot travel through a vacuum. Solids, liquids and gases all provide particles for propagation.

items.stem: The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of one kilogram of a substance by one kelvin is called its
items.explanation: Specific heat capacity is the heat needed per unit mass per unit rise in temperature. Latent heat is absorbed at a change of state without a temperature change, thermal conductivity measures heat flow, and emissivity describes radiation.

items.stem: An adiabatic process in thermodynamics is one in which
options: The temperature of the system stays constant
The pressure of the system stays constant
No heat is exchanged between the system and its surroundings
The volume of the system stays constant
items.explanation: An adiabatic process is defined by zero heat transfer, so the first law reduces to a change in internal energy equal to minus the work done. Constant temperature, pressure and volume describe isothermal, isobaric and isochoric processes respectively.

items.stem: The electric field at a distance of 0.3 m from a point charge of 1 microcoulomb in air is (k = 9 x 10^9 N m^2 C^-2)
items.explanation: E = k q / r^2 = 9e9 times 1e-6 divided by 0.09 = 1e5 N per coulomb. Forgetting to square the distance or misplacing the decimal gives the distractors.

items.stem: Three resistors of 2 ohm each are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the combination is
items.explanation: For n equal resistors in parallel R_eq = R/n = 2/3 ohm. Adding them as if in series gives 6 ohm, which is the series value rather than the parallel value.

items.stem: A charged particle moves parallel to a uniform magnetic field. The magnetic force acting on it is
options: Equal to the product of charge, speed and field strength
items.explanation: The force is F = q v B sin(theta) where theta is the angle between velocity and field. When they are parallel theta is zero, the sine is zero, and the force vanishes; the maximum occurs when the motion is perpendicular to the field.

items.stem: The power of a convex lens of focal length 0.5 m, expressed in dioptres, is
items.explanation: Power is the reciprocal of focal length in metres, so P = 1/0.5 = 2 dioptres. Reporting the focal length itself or misplacing the decimal gives the other values.

items.stem: The energy of the electron in the ground state of a hydrogen atom is
items.explanation: The ground state energy of hydrogen is -13.6 eV, the negative sign showing that the electron is bound. The energies -3.4 eV and -1.51 eV belong to the first and second excited states, and a positive value would mean an unbound electron.
